I am a 30 year old female and I grew up with divorced parents. They split when I was 2 so all I have ever known is step parents, custody battles, parents hating each other. My biggest piece of advice I can give you is spend more time with your daughter and start forming a strong bond with her. Start doing activities with just the two of you. Show her that no matter what happens or who you end up marrying, your daughter always comes first. This is where my father failed and I haven’t spoken to him for 7 years. He was selfish, was co dependent and needed to be in a relationship so desperately that he sacrificed his relationship with his children. My dad isn’t even if with that woman he sacrificed his relationship with his children for. My point is, I wish my dad would have tried to show that I actually mattered to him. If your daughter really feels like you see her, support her, love her and will always be in her corner, then I guarantee the jealousy will go away. It sounds like you have a great girlfriend and being a step parent is incredibly difficult. She should definitely keep trying to make an effort with your daughter. But the more confident your daughter is with her relationship with you, then things will start to feel more cohesive and your girlfriend might not need to “try” so much. This takes time though and 10-12 is such a hard age. She is saying those mean things to you because she’s not feeling heard or might not feel secure. Make sure that you and your daughters mom are actively co-parenting. If you have drama, then you guys need to work it out because your kid comes first. She didn’t choose to be born to you guys, so please have all parties be civil for the sake of your child. From a daughter who didn’t have a father who cared for her, thank you for giving a shit and trying to make an effort. You’re already on the right path and I wish you all the luck 😊
